author: J.F.Gmelin, 1789

art.subject: Black Bulbul (Hypsipetes leucocephalus), adult of the white-headed form (sexes alike, plumage similar year-round): entire head, throat and neck pure white, the white ending sharply on the upper breast and lower nape; the rest of the plumage, including back, wings, breast, belly, undertail coverts and tail, uniform sooty black to dark slate-grey without pattern; bill bright coral-red; dark brown eye; legs and feet bright coral-red.
art.pose: perched upright on a bare treetop branch, side view
art.scene: evergreen broadleaf trees on a southern Korean offshore island in early spring, bright daylight; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A slim, medium-sized bulbul, slightly smaller and slimmer than a Brown-eared Bulbul, with a rounded head that may look slightly bushy at the rear. Bill medium, a little shorter than the head, fairly slender with a slightly curved tip. Legs short. Wingtips at rest fall well short of the tail tip; the tail is fairly long and shallowly forked. Perches upright on exposed treetops; flight undulating, often in noisy flocks.
avoid: Do not paint a grey-brown body with chestnut ear patches; that is Brown-eared Bulbul (Hypsipetes amaurotis).
Do not make the bill or legs black, yellow or orange; both are bright coral-red.
Do not add black on the head or a dark eye-mask; in this form the whole head is white.
Do not paint a tall pointed crest; the head is rounded.
